name: Psilocybin
summary: Psilocybin is inactive. It is a phosphate ester that exists, as far as the mushroom is concerned, to be stable — and the moment it meets the phosphatases in your gut wall and liver it loses that phosphate and becomes psilocin, which is the actual drug. Everything you feel is psilocin; psilocybin is the packaging.
model_note: The curve tracks psilocin, the active species. Dephosphorylation is fast relative to absorption, so the rise you see is dominated by how quickly the mushroom material is digested — which is why the onset varies so much with stomach contents and preparation.
mechanism: Psilocin is a 5-HT2A agonist, structurally close to serotonin itself. The same receptor as LSD, but with much faster dissociation, which is why the experience is roughly half as long despite comparable intensity.

oral.note: Eaten as dried mushroom, where the drug has to be released from fungal tissue before anything can be absorbed — which is why onset ranges from 20 minutes to well over an hour and why an empty stomach makes it faster and sharper.

oral_tea.note: Extracted into hot water first, so absorption begins immediately. Faster onset, often less nausea, same total exposure.

metabolism.primary_enzyme: Alkaline phosphatase, then UGT1A10 and MAO

pathways.name: Psilocin glucuronide
pathways.note: The main route out. Inactive and renally excreted; this is what urine testing would look for, though psilocin is not on standard panels.

pathways.name: 4-hydroxyindole-3-acetic acid
pathways.note: Via monoamine oxidase — the same enzyme that handles serotonin.

risk: Mushroom potency varies by several fold between species, specimens and even parts of the same mushroom, so a dose in grams is a much rougher measure than a dose in milligrams. The presets here assume roughly 1% psilocybin by dry weight, which is an average, not a guarantee.
Misidentification of wild mushrooms is the serious physical danger — some lethal species are superficially similar, and liver failure from amatoxins begins after a symptom-free day.
Like LSD, the physiological margin is wide and the real risks are psychological and situational. Pre-existing psychosis risk is the main contraindication.
Lithium is associated with seizures in combination. SSRIs blunt the effect, and MAOIs — including those in some ayahuasca preparations — substantially intensify and prolong it. See interactions.
